parts.stem: Solutions of Group 2 hydrogencarbonates, $\text{M}(\text{HCO}_3)_2$, decompose on heating to give the corresponding metal carbonate, carbon dioxide and water.
parts.text: Write an equation for the decomposition of strontium hydrogencarbonate, $\text{Sr}(\text{HCO}_3)_2$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The thermal stability of Group 2 carbonates increases down the group.

Explain this trend.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The hydroxides and fluorides of Group 2 elements show similar trends in solubility.

Describe the trend in the solubility of the fluorides of calcium, strontium and barium.

Explain your answer.

parts.text:
State the main factors that affect the magnitude of enthalpy change of hydration.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Table 1.1 shows various energy changes.

Table 1.1

| energy change | value / $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| lattice energy of $\text{MgF}_2$ | $-2957$ |
| enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$, of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ | $-1926$ |
| enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$, of $\text{F}^{-}$ | $-505$ |

Use data from Table 1.1 to calculate the enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H_{\text{sol}}$, for $\text{MgF}_2(\text{s})$.

It may be helpful to draw a labelled energy cycle. Show your working.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
Mercury(I) fluoride, $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$, is sparingly soluble in water.

The cation in $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$ exists as the diatomic ion $\text{Hg}_2^{2+}$ with a covalent $\text{Hg-Hg}$ bond.
parts.text: Write the expression for the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$. Include the units.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
The solubility of $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$ is $9.20 \times 10^{-3} \text{mol dm}^{-3}$ at $298 \text{ K}$.

Calculate the value of $K_{\text{sp}}$ of $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$ at $298 \text{ K}$.
